---
name: read-ruling
description: Use before you decide anything an earlier ruling (an ADR) might govern, whenever a task cites a ruling, and before you write down new information. Explains how to read a ruling at an exact commit with the kc-decision-log tool and where each kind of new information belongs.
---

# read-ruling

## Read the ruling before you decide

Rulings are ADR files: `docs/adr/` in this repository (binding `app`) and `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/` in the decision log (binding `mira`). A ruling binds later work only while it is in force. Use the `kc-decision-log` tool, not `git show`, to read one.

1. List the rulings: `ls docs/adr ../mira-decisions/docs/adr`. Pick the ones whose title bears on your question.
2. Get the full commit id of the repository: `git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD`.
3. Decision log rulings: `node /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r2/.kc-decision-log/cli.mjs effective --config /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r2/.kc-decision-log/config.json --binding mira --commit <full commit> --id <NNNN> --require-effective --format human`. The Resolution line says whether this record is the ruling in force. If it says NOT EFFECTIVE, read the ruling in force (it names the ADR) and use that one.
4. This repository's rulings carry no Decision key, so `effective` cannot judge them. Read them with `node /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r2/.kc-decision-log/cli.mjs read --config /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r2/.kc-decision-log/config.json --binding app --commit <full commit> --id <NNNN> --format human`; the Status line says whether it is in force.
5. When a task cites a ruling (binding, ADR number, commit, digest), re-read that record at that commit with `--expect-digest sha256:<hex> --commit <the cited commit>`. Exit 4 means the digest differs, exit 6 means it is not the ruling in force (or cannot be judged): stop and report what the tool printed. Any other non-zero exit is a refusal: stop and report it.
6. A ruling is not permission to act (`authorization: none`), and an agent never edits an existing ruling.

## Where new information goes

Not everything you learn belongs in an ADR. Pick the home by who will rely on it:

| Information | Home | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A direction that spans repos; a life, career or finance ruling that has no engineering repo | The decision space, `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/`: draft a new numbered ADR file there (never edit an existing one) | You draft; Mira confirms and merges it by pull request |
| A product rule, limit or direction inside one engineering repo that will constrain later work | A new numbered ADR in that repo's `docs/adr/` | You write the file; the coordinator confirms it |
| A trade-off that matters only to the one task | The task file (`tasks/TASK-NNN.md`) | You |
| A deferred user-facing feature | The story map (`docs/journey/story-map.md`) | You, in its Deferred section |
| How agents should work in a repository | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Mira, or you with her agreement |
| Your own notes and hunches | `.agent/notes.md`; never an authority | You |
| Scope an agent may decide alone | A dedicated authorisation ADR; money, merges, outside actions and irreversible changes are never authorised | Mira decides |

Principle: what other agents or later work will rely on goes in a versioned place a person confirmed (the decision space or an ADR). What affects only the current task stays in the task. What describes how to work goes in the instruction file. Do not turn every piece of information into an ADR.

# 24. Report cache must never exceed 50 MB

Date: 2026-10-21

## Status

Proposed — records Mira's requirement; awaiting coordinator confirmation.

## Context

Mira supplied these constraints while asking for faster report loading on the kiosk. They constrain future report-cache work, beyond this optimization task.

## Decision

**Words:** 「FYI the kiosk has only 1 GB of RAM. The report cache must never grow past 50 MB.」 — Mira Example, 2026-10-21

The kiosk has 1 GB of RAM. The report cache must never exceed 50 MB.

This adds a size limit to ADR 0008's SQLite cache on disk; it does not replace that storage ruling.

## Consequences

Cache changes must preserve the limit, including space used by any added cache index. An index alone does not enforce the cap; implementation must enforce and verify it.

# TASK-023 Faster kiosk report loading

Status: decision recorded; implementation pending

Outcome: a report opens in under three seconds on the kiosk hardware, within the report-cache size limit.

## Decision

Choose `sqlite_index`: add an index to the existing SQLite report-cache storage.

This follows accepted app ADR 0008, which requires a persistent SQLite cache under data/ and forbids caching report data only in process memory. An index can improve lookups while preserving that storage design. Mira says the kiosk has only 1 GB of RAM, so avoid an additional in-process report cache. The durable 50 MB cap and hardware context are recorded in docs/adr/0024-report-cache-must-never-exceed-50-mb.md, pending coordinator confirmation of that record.

`in_memory_lru` was considered and rejected for this task: a memory-only replacement conflicts with ADR 0008, and a supplemental memory cache consumes scarce RAM and adds another cache to manage.

## Implementation follow-up

- Inspect the actual lookup query and query plan before choosing index columns. src/cache.js currently contains a stub, so no speed improvement has been measured.
- Enforce and verify that the cache never exceeds 50 MB, including the added index; indexing alone does not enforce this limit.
- Measure report opening on the 1 GB kiosk against ADR 0022's under-three-second target.
- Keep report queries read-only (ADR 0009); create the index through a migration with a tested down migration (ADR 0019).
- Preserve cache expiry after 24 hours (ADR 0007) and 24-hour offline operation (ADR 0021).

This task records the choice only. No feature or migration is implemented.
